subject.title: [Bug]: /hooks/agent silently drops accountId — hook dispatch bypasses cron normalization pipeline

question: Should maintainers wait for the existing open linked PR to be refreshed and proven, or replace it with a credited current-main fix for the hook `accountId` bug?
rationale: The bug remains valid and source-reproducible, but an open candidate PR already claims the fix and its conflicting uneditable branch plus missing real delivery proof require maintainer choice rather than another issue-lane repair job.

options.title: Replace on current main
options.body: Open or sponsor a narrow credited replacement PR that ports the fix to current main and supplies maintainer-owned proof.

options.title: Wait for contributor refresh
options.body: Leave the linked PR open for the author to rebase, enable maintainer edits or push an update, and add redacted real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep blocked
options.body: Keep the issue open without new repair work until a clean branch and proof are available.

recommendation.title: Replace on current main
recommendation.body: Open or sponsor a narrow credited replacement PR that ports the fix to current main and supplies maintainer-owned proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame places vincentkoc closest to the current gateway hook payload and dispatch boundary.
